The song "I Still Haven't Found What I'm Looking For" is sung by the Irish rock band U2.
Is this song popular? did it get nominated for any awards?

Yes, the song "I Still Haven't Found What I'm Looking For" by U2 was quite popular. It became the band's second consecutive number-one single on the US Billboard Hot 100 and peaked at number six on the UK Singles Chart. The song was also critically acclaimed and received two nominations at the 30th Annual Grammy Awards in 1988, for Record of the Year and Song of the Year. It has since become one of the group's most well-known songs and has been performed on many of their concert tours. Additionally, it has appeared on several of their compilations and concert films. Many critics and publications have ranked the song among the greatest tracks in music history, including Rolling Stone which placed it at number 93 on its list of "The 500 Greatest Songs of All Time."
There is also a 1990 dance remake of the song by the Scottish band The Chimes, which became a UK Top Ten hit.
"I Still Haven't Found What I'm Looking For" music video

The music video for "I Still Haven't Found What I'm Looking For" was filmed on Fremont Street in Las Vegas on April 12, 1987. It was made after U2's Joshua Tree Tour concert in the city. The video shows the band members wandering around while the Edge plays an acoustic guitar. The music video was later released on The U218 Videos compilation DVD. Pat Christenson, president of Las Vegas's official event organization, has credited the group's video with improving the city's image among musicians.
how was the song  "I Still Haven't Found What I'm Looking For" created?

The song "I Still Haven't Found What I'm Looking For" was created during a jam session by the band U2 at the studio they had set up at Danesmoate House in Dublin. The initial idea for the song came from a demo titled "The Weather Girls" or "Under the Weather," which had a drum part played by drummer Larry Mullen Jr. that the band found interesting. Co-producer Daniel Lanois encouraged Mullen to develop this unusual drum pattern, which became the root of the song.
The Edge wrote a chord sequence and played it on acoustic guitar, and the group tried out various vocal melody ideas. During the jam session, Bono began singing a "classic soul" melody, which made the Edge hear the song's potential. Bono was inspired by a line from the Bob Dylan song "Idiot Wind" and suggested the phrase "I still have n't found what I 'm looking for" as a possible song title.
As recording continued, the band added various guitar overdubs, including an auto-pan effect and a chiming arpeggio. Bono sang in the upper register of his range, and background vocals were provided by the Edge, Lanois, and co-producer Brian Eno. Lanois also played a percussive guitar part heard in the introduction.
The song's writing was completed early during the band's time at Danesmoate House, but the mix took longer to complete. The final mix was completed by Lanois and the Edge in a home studio set up at Melbeach, a house purchased by the Edge. They mixed it on top of a previous Steve Lillywhite mix, which gave the song a phasing sound.
what do people think about this song?

"I Still Haven't Found What I'm Looking For" by U2 received widespread critical acclaim. Hot Press journalist Bill Graham described the song as a "smart job of pop handwork" and "pretty standard American radio rock - ballad fare," but praised the band's "supple and cultivated" rhythms. The Sunday Independent suggested that the song proved the band could be commercially accessible without resorting to rock clichés. NME remarked that the song showed that the band cared about something, making them "special." The Rocket noted that Bono's lyrics about personal spirituality resulted in a "unique marriage of American gospel and Gaelic soul." Several publications, including The Bergen Record and The Boston Globe, called the track "hypnotic" and interpreted it as depicting the band on a spiritual quest. The song finished in 18th place on The Village Voice's "Best Singles" list from its 1987 Pazz & Jop critics' poll.
